items.name: narration_en
items.direction: Narrate this for a premium documentary YouTube Shorts channel about money, history and the tricks behind them. The Narrator is a deep, warm, confident storyteller with a hint of mystery: curious, quietly amused, energetic and punchy, never slow, never announcer-like. Natural emphasis on dates and numbers, questions end with a curious lift, a short comic pause before each punchline. Keep the same voice, pace and energy from start to finish. Chars voices two funny cartoon characters (a smug gold bar and a nervous banknote), short and punchy, performed exactly as described in each bracket.
lines: Narrator
Every penny in your change cost America almost four cents to make. So why keep making it?
Narrator
In twenty twenty-four, the Mint spent about three point seven cents on each one-cent coin. A loss on every single one.
Chars
[smug, deep, rich gold bar, very pleased with himself] Losing money to make money. Bold.
Narrator
So why didn't they stop sooner?
Narrator
Pennies go back to seventeen ninety-three. Habit, tradition, and partly a fear that shops would round prices up.
Narrator
Then the Treasury placed its final order for penny blanks.
Narrator
The last one was struck in Philadelphia in November twenty twenty-five.
Narrator
And here's the coin that's even worse.
Narrator
The nickel also costs more than five cents to make. And it's still being made.
Narrator
That's the mirage: a coin's value is printed on it, not built into it.
Narrator
Over a hundred and fourteen billion pennies are still out there, still legal tender.
Chars
[delighted, squeaky banknote, surprised to be winning] Finally, a coin with a worse job than me!
Narrator
Comment: do you still use pennies?
Narrator
This is Money Mirage. Follow for more.
